title: Plants and People
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Plants and People Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Assess ways people use and depend on plants, including Indigenous knowledge such as the Three Sisters; describe plant adaptations; evaluate ways to protect plants and their habitats. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Growth and Changes in Plants)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on how people use plants, the Three Sisters, maple syrup, plant adaptations and caring for plants. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Plants give us food, oxygen, medicine and materials, so we must protect them.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants give us food, oxygen, shade, medicine, clothing and building materials.

  • Many Indigenous communities grow the Three Sisters: corn, beans and squash, which help each other.
  • Plants have adaptations, like thick stems to store water or wide leaves to catch light.
  • We protect plants by caring for habitats, planting native plants and stopping invasive species.
Example

Which tree gives sap for maple syrup?

sugar maple

Answer: the sugar maple

Example

How do beans help the Three Sisters?

they add nutrients to the soil

Answer: they feed the soil

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all plants are safe to eat.
  • Thinking plants are not living things.
  • Thinking people do not need plants.

faq.a: They make oxygen and food, give habitat to animals and give people many materials and medicines.
Corn, beans and squash, grown together in many Indigenous traditions because they help each other grow.
Stay on trails, do not pick wildflowers in parks, plant native plants and remove invasive plants.

items.q: Which part of the plant do we eat when we eat kale?

items.q: How do beans help corn and squash in a Three Sisters garden?

items.q: What is an invasive plant?

a plant that lives inside a house

a plant that is very small
items.e: Garlic mustard is invasive in Ontario.

items.q: A plant is kept in a dark cupboard, so its leaves get no light. What will most likely happen to the plant?
c: It cannot take in water, so it wilts.
It cannot make seeds for new plants.
Water cannot reach the leaves, so they dry up.
It cannot make its food, so it grows weakly.
items.e: Each part does a job the plant needs.

items.q: A rose bush has sharp thorns on its stems. How does this structure help the plant?
c: It helps with spreading seeds far away on the wind.
It helps with growing tall above other plants to get sunlight.
It helps with keeping animals from eating it.
It helps with surviving cold, snowy winters.
items.e: This structure is suited to keeping animals from eating it.

items.q: A plant's roots are cut off. What will most likely happen to the plant?

It cannot take in water, so it wilts.
items.e: Each part does a job the plant needs.

items.q: Why are bees important to farmers?

items.e: No pollination means fewer fruits.

items.q: A coconut palm has fruits that can float on the ocean. How does this structure help the plant?
c: It helps with spreading seeds to new islands.
It helps with spreading seeds far away on the wind.

items.e: This structure is suited to spreading seeds to new islands.

items.q: What can people do to protect plants in a park?

items.q: Which is a way people use plants?

items.e: Plants are very important to people.

items.q: Why should you wash fruit from the store before eating it?

items.q: How do seeds with hooks travel?

items.q: Which part of a plant carries water up to the leaves?

items.q: What is seed dispersal?
c: seeds moving away from the parent plant
items.e: Seeds travel to new places.

items.q: Why is it good for seeds to travel?
c: They grow better under the parent plant.
They have more room, light and water to grow.
items.e: Less crowding.

items.q: Does a seed need fertilizer to germinate?
c: Yes. A seed cannot germinate without it.
No. A seed can germinate without it.
Yes, but only in the day.
items.e: Seeds can germinate on wet cotton balls in the dark. They need minerals from the soil later, when the young plant grows.

items.e: Models help us explain.

items.q: Which part of a plant takes in water?

items.q: Which way does water travel in a plant?

items.q: Which part of the plant takes in nutrients from the soil?

items.q: Do plants need air?

items.q: Why do plants need water?

items.e: Wilting means thirsty.

Only seeds planted in pots need it.
items.e: Seeds germinate when they have water, air and a suitable temperature.

items.q: Why do bees visit flowers?

items.q: Which season do most plants in Ontario grow fastest?

items.q: What happens to a plant that does not get enough water?
